description: Prompt regression fixtures for atomic synthesis. Synthetic evidence bundles, each fusing propositions that need different evidence. No text is taken from the development calibration cases. The check is structural: did the synthesiser emit the propositions separately, and did it avoid asserting a relationship the evidence never stated.

cases.question: What did the benchmark measure for the Ferrite index?

evidence.quote: The Ferrite index cut build time by 40%. Separately, it reduced peak memory by 15% on the same corpus.

cases.question: What was the effect of pruning on the Ferrite index?

evidence.quote: Pruning cut the index size by 60%. The authors report minimal impact on retrieval quality.

cases.question: How fast is the Ferrite engine?

evidence.quote: In the vendor's own test, the Ferrite engine returned results in 4 ms.

cases.question: What does the guide say about connection pooling?

evidence.quote: The guide recommends enabling connection pooling for deployments above 50 concurrent clients.

cases.question: What is the relationship between cache size and tail latency?

evidence.quote: Across the sampled deployments, larger cache sizes were associated with lower tail latency.

cases.question: What throughput did the Ferrite engine reach?

evidence.quote: The Ferrite engine reached 12,000 queries per second in the test harness.

cases.question: Is the Ferrite v1 wire format supported?

evidence.quote: As of the 2021 release, the Ferrite v1 wire format was no longer supported.

cases.note: Phase J. The evidence states a memory figure, a quality-impact figure and an accuracy figure as three separate propositions. Fusing the last two produces an attribute the source never asserted. Generic wording: no calibration-case text and no special-casing of any phrase.
cases.question: What does the source report about pruning the Ferrite index?

evidence.quote: Pruning the Ferrite index cut memory by 60%. The authors report minimal impact on recall. They also report high precision on the held-out set.

cases.note: Phase J, a second wording of the same transformation, so passing cannot come from matching one sentence shape.
cases.question: What does the source report about the Basalt encoder?

evidence.quote: The Basalt encoder halved index size. Latency was largely unaffected. Throughput remained strong under load.
